name: Leeks
frostTenderNotes: Not stated directly by the sourced KZN DARD documents. Leeks are grown through the coldest 'Cold areas / Moderate frosts' window (Nov-Apr, spanning the hard-frost May-Aug period's lead-up and tail) per Table 6, implying meaningful cold tolerance, but no explicit minimum-temperature or frost-damage statement was found, so left null rather than inferred.

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Source gives a single figure (150 days), not a range, unlike most other crops in the same table; no '*' marker so it is unclear whether this is from sowing or transplanting. A Starke Ayres home-garden catalogue separately markets an onion (not leek) cultivar at 155 days for comparison, but no leek entry was found in that catalogue, so no seed-company cross-check exists for leek maturity.

rowSpacingRangeCm.notes: Source gives a single row-spacing figure (300mm), not a range.

seedRateKgPerHaRange.notes: 4kg/ha (seedbed, for raising transplants) to 8kg/ha (direct field sowing); the 0.7-1.5kg seedtray figure is left out of the range as it is a lower-volume specialised-nursery method, not a field-scale rate.

yield.notes: KZN DARD's 'Expected Yields' Table 8 runs alphabetically from Lettuce directly to Marrow with no Leek row — confirmed absent, not overlooked. A South African DAFF-authored leek article was located via a Senwes 'Crops and Markets' quarterly (2010), which states leek production is a year-round SA enterprise, but the hosting domain (www2.senwes.co.za) is blocked by this environment's network egress and could not be fetched to extract or verify any yield figure. No other SA study (ARC, university) with a leek field-trial yield could be found. DAFF/DALRRD's own brochure archive could not be checked in this pass either: the Wayback Machine was returning 'Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline' for the whole domain, and dalrrd.gov.za/nda.agric.za direct connections failed (502/connection-reset), both confirmed to be transient infrastructure issues at the time of this search rather than a confirmed absence of the document. Recorded as a genuine, still-open gap pending a retry when those sources are reachable again.

ecocropNotes: EcoCrop_DB.csv has no row for Allium ampeloprasum, Allium porrum, or any leek-labelled entry; only Allium cepa, A. fistulosum and A. cepa var. aggregatum rows exist, none of which is leek's own species, so left null rather than substituting a different Allium species' climate envelope.
varietiesNotes: No SA seed-company catalogue with a dedicated leek entry was located in this research pass (the Starke Ayres home-garden catalogue checked covers onion and spring onion cultivars but has no leek section), and neither DAFF nor the KZN DARD documents used name any leek cultivars. Recorded as a gap rather than inventing cultivar names.

zoneNotes.highveld: KZN's 'Cold areas / Moderate frosts' window (Nov-Apr) applies per the sourced 3-tier table.
zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: Falls under 'Hot areas / Frost-free' (Mar-Apr) per the sourced table — a narrow window compared with the other zones.
zoneNotes.subtropical-coast: Falls under 'Hot areas / Frost-free' (Mar-Apr) by the same table; not separately confirmed.
zoneNotes.midlands-mistbelt: KZN's own 'Warm areas / Light frosts' window (Sept-Oct, Feb-May) applies directly.
zoneNotes.western-cape: Not covered by a Western Cape-specific source; 'winter' sowMonths inferred equal to 'summer' — flagged gap.
zoneNotes.high-mountain: Not confirmed by source; the crop's long 150-day cycle through the Cold-areas window suggests it endures real frost, but no direct statement covers this zone specifically.

gaps: No yield (t/ha) figure found for leek in any sourced KZN DARD document — confirmed absent from the 'Expected Yields' table rather than overlooked. A relevant Senwes/DAFF article exists but its host is blocked in this research environment; DAFF/DALRRD's own archive was unreachable during this pass due to a Wayback Machine outage and direct nda.agric.za/dalrrd.gov.za connection failures -- see yield.notes.
No named SA leek cultivars sourced from any seed catalogue, DAFF or KZN document checked.
No Western Cape/winter-rainfall-specific sowing calendar found; 'winter' sowMonths inferred equal to 'summer'.
frostTender left null — no explicit cold-tolerance statement found for leek specifically.
No EcoCrop row exists for Allium ampeloprasum/porrum in the available database copy.
The 150-day days-to-harvest figure is a single point value, not a range, and it is unclear whether it is measured from sowing or from transplanting.
summary: Sourced from KZN DARD's 'Plant Establishment' and 'Length of Growing Period' chapters: sowMonths (all four rain-pattern columns via the Cold/Warm/Hot 3-tier table), row/in-row spacing, sow depth, seed rate and a single days-to-harvest figure (150 days) are directly quoted. Verdict is 'partial' because no yield (t/ha) figure exists for leek in the KZN 'Expected Yields' table (confirmed absent) and no named SA cultivars could be sourced from any catalogue checked.
